import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# The dataset contains future dates for data releases. Filter for historical, complete years.
# Assuming the script is run in 2024, the last complete year is 2023.
current_year = pd.Timestamp.now().year
df_filtered = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] < current_year].copy()

# Determine the date range for the title
min_year = df_filtered['StichtagDatJahr'].min()
max_year = df_filtered['StichtagDatJahr'].max()

# Clean up breed names by stripping leading/trailing whitespace
df_filtered['Rasse1Text'] = df_filtered['Rasse1Text'].str.strip()

# Identify the top 10 most popular breeds in the most recent available year for relevance
latest_year_data = df_filtered[df_filtered['StichtagDatJahr'] == max_year]
top_10_breeds = latest_year_data['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the entire historical dataset to include only these top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df_filtered[df_filtered['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)].copy()

# Group by year and breed to get the annual registration count
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='Anzahl')

# Ensure breed names are treated as a categorical type with a consistent order for plotting
breed_trends['Rasse1Text'] = pd.Categorical(breed_trends['Rasse1Text'], categories=top_10_breeds, ordered=True)
breed_trends = breed_trends.sort_values('Rasse1Text')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style and a color-blind friendly palette
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.facecolor": "#f7f7f7", "figure.facecolor": "#f7f7f7"})
palette = sns.color_palette("tab10", n_colors=10)

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))

# Create the line plot to show trends over time
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='Anzahl',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    style='Rasse1Text',
    palette=palette,
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    lw=2.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labels ---

# Set a clear title and axis labels
ax.set_title(
    f'Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({int(min_year)}-{int(max_year)})',
    fontsize=20, pad=25, weight='bold', loc='left'
)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Improve tick label appearance and grid lines
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12, length=0)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(integer=True))
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='-', alpha=0.9)
ax.set_frame_on(False)

# Customize and position the legend outside the plot area
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=13,
    frameon=False
)

# Add a data source annotation
fig.text(0.99, 0.01, 'Source: Stadt Zürich, Open Data',
         ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=10, color='gray')

# Save the final figure, using bbox_inches='tight' to ensure all elements are included
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
